entries.proposition: Cohort: eight patients with COL4A2-related infantile epileptic spasm syndrome, trio exome sequencing, ACMG classification; patients with significant structural abnormality excluded.
entries.snippet: Patients with epilepsy caused by intrauterine infection, perinatal brain injury, metabolic disease, or significant brain structural abnormalities were not included in the study.

entries.proposition: Genetics: eight missense variants, seven likely pathogenic and one (patient 7, c.1838G>T, p.G613V) of uncertain significance; the variant chosen for the functional work is the uncertain one, inherited from a mother with intellectual disability but no epilepsy.
entries.snippet: Genetic analysis revealed eight missense mutations related to Col4a2 infantile epileptic spasm syndrome, seven of which are likely pathogenic and the other one is of uncertain significance (Table 2).

entries.proposition: Text: GFAP expression rose after the mutation in primary astrocytes by IF and western, indicating increased astrocyte activity.
entries.snippet: Our results revealed a significant increase in GFAP expression following Col4a2 mutation in both CTX-TNA cells (IF: p<0.001; Fig. 1A, B, F) and primary astrocytes (IF: p = 0.0017; Fig. 3A, B, F), indicating increased astrocyte activity.
entries.anchor: Results, Col4a2 mutation promotes astrocyte activation

entries.proposition: The wild-type vector is said to reduce inflammation, suggesting a protective role for the wild-type gene; the comparison is overexpression of wild type against overexpression of the variant in LPS-stimulated cells, with no knockdown or null.
entries.snippet: These findings suggest that excessive astrocyte activation can trigger inflammatory responses. Mutation of Col4a2 enhanced the secretion of inflammatory cytokines, while overexpression of Col4a2Wt protected against inflammation.

entries.snippet: However, the specific mechanism by which Col4a2 mutation triggers JAK/STAT activation remains unclear.
